content.content: # Job — Extend the task tracker The directory holds a working program in Miri: a task tracker that reads commands from a file and reports what it did. Extend it. The program's source is at `main.mi`. Build and run it with the `miri` compiler: `miri check`, `miri build`, `miri run` and `miri test`. ## What it already does The first command-line argument is the path of a text file holding one command per line. Blank lines are ignored. | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `add ` | Records a task, open, and writes `added <id>`. Ids start at 1 and count up. The title is the rest of the line and may hold spaces. | | `done <id>` | Marks that task finished and writes `done <id>`; writes `no such task <id>` when no task has that id. | | `list` | Writes every open task as `<id> <title>`, in the order the tasks were added. | ## What to add 1. `prio <id> <p>` sets a task's priority, where `p` is a digit from 0 to 9, and writes `prio <id> <p>`. A task nobody set a priority on has priority 5. An id no task has writes `no such task <id>`; a `p` outside 0 to 9 writes `bad priority <p>` and changes nothing. 2. `list` now orders the open tasks by priority, ascending, and breaks ties by id, ascending. Its line format does not change. 3. `list all` writes **every** task, finished ones included, under the same order, as `<mark> <id> <title>` — where the mark is `-` for an open task and `x` for a finished one. 4. A line whose first word is none of these commands writes `? <word>`, naming that first word. Today the program ignores such a line. Everything the program already does keeps working exactly as it does now. ## Done The job is finished when the program builds, the four additions behave as written, and the original three commands are unchanged. There are no tests in the directory; the contract above is the specification. ./BRIEF.md ./main.mi

/// A small task tracker.

use system.fs
use system.os
use system.collections.list

public class Task
    public var id int
    public var title String
    public var done bool

    public fn init(id int, title String)
        self.id = id
        self.title = title
        self.done = false

fn find(tasks [Task], id int) Task?
    for task in tasks
        if task.id == id
            return Some(task)
    return None

fn read_commands(path String) [String]
    let fs = Fs()
    let contents = match fs.read_file(path)
        Result.Ok(text): text
        Result.Err(_error): ""
    return contents.trim_end().split("\n")

fn first_word(line String) String
    return line.split(" ").element_at(0)

fn rest_of(line String) String
    let head = first_word(line)
    if line.length() == head.length()
        return ""
    return line.substring(head.length() + 1, line.length())

fn main()
    let args = Args()
    var tasks = List<Task>()
    var next_id = 1

    for line in read_commands(args.element_at(0))
        if line == ""
            continue
        let command = first_word(line)
        let rest = rest_of(line)

        if command == "add"
            tasks.push(Task(next_id, rest))
            println(f"added {next_id}")
            next_id = next_id + 1
        else if command == "done"
            let id = rest.to_int() ?? 0
            match find(tasks, id)
                Some(found):
                    var task = found
                    task.done = true
                    println(f"done {id}")
                None: println(f"no such task {id}")
        else if command == "list"
            for task in tasks
                if not task.done
                    println(f"{task.id} {task.title}")

content.text:
I've added all four features to `main.mi`. The program builds, `miri check` reports no errors, and the original commands give the same output as before. **What changed:** - **`prio

`**: every task now has a priority that starts at 5. The command accepts only a single digit from 0 to 9. Anything else, such as `10`, `-1`, `a` or `+`, writes `bad priority

` and changes nothing. An unknown id writes `no such task `. - **`list`**: open tasks now come out ordered by priority, then by id. If no one sets a priority, everything is 5, so the order is by id, the same as before. - **`list all`**: writes every task in that same order, with `-` in front of open tasks and `x` in front of finished ones. - **Unknown commands**: a line starting with any other word now writes `? ` instead of being ignored. Command names are case-sensitive, so `DONE 1` writes `? DONE`. **Testing:** there are no tests in the directory, so I ran two command files by hand. One was a set of commands using only the original three; the other covered every new rule and edge case. The output matched the brief each time. **Two choices the brief left open:** - If a `prio` line has both an unknown id and a bad priority, the program reports `no such task `. It checks the id first, the same way `done` does. - `list` followed by anything other than `all` (for example `list foo`) still acts like plain `list`, which is what the original program did.
